correctness.rationale: Both the frozen mathematics and the repaired equality classification are correct. Period one and reflection reduce t to [0,1/2]; sorting loses only permutations. On each crossing cell the frozen projection argument is valid: every fixed-center quadratic is a global upper bound on the pointwise nearest-center distance, and an incident cell at a minimizing time uses a nearest center even at a tied endpoint. Recomputing the exemplar gives Q=306, minimum numerator 576, and the two half-period times 8/51 and 25/51. Rescaling t leaves the score unchanged under doubling. Independently of the frozen enumeration, the repair partitions the sorted vectors by their last coordinate h and uses a fixed 90-cell common refinement, minimizing each quadratic on its own closed interval by exact clipping. The interval rejection test is strict: it drops only vectors already below 8/17, and evaluates all intervals of each survivor. Integer sizes are bounded since Q,B,C≤4608 and all endpoint denominators are at most 24; simultaneous crossings and repeats do not cause special cases. The four replay chunks visited 203490, 1358785, 2729870 and 3596580 tuples, totaling 7888725, the required binomial count. Only (1,2,3,4,5,7,9,11) and its double survived, both at exactly 8/17. Only the first is primitive. No uniqueness statement beyond the box is made.
residual_risks: The certificate covers precisely positive integer vectors of height at most 24 and does not independently prove an unbounded-height theorem.

value.rationale: For the narrowed claim, the height cap is the established six-dimensional validation budget applied to the now-solved eight-dimensional value. Given the global optimum, a distinct practical and mathematical question is which positive integer multisets under that budget can attain it, including whether exactly one primitive orbit suffices or other repeated-coordinate types occur. The exact classification and strict exclusion of all alternatives answer that question, and are not a recomputation credited merely because it reproduces the known numerical maximum. The result is a finite uniqueness benchmark, not an unrestricted classification.
residual_risks: The original optimum/lower-bound headline has no separate contribution after the stronger result. The remaining benchmark is tied to the motivated cap and its equality problem, not arbitrary larger heights.
